body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — past, future, and present!

children.translated_text: [<s>mantra</s> continued:] guruṇi cale mucale samucale guhaṇi-guhaṇi guruṇi-guruṇi culu-culu cale-cale mucale — O Victorious One (<s>jayavijaye</s>), O Ever-Victorious (<s>jayavati</s>), O Invincible One (<s>aparājita</s>), you from whom all fear has departed (<s>sarvabhayavigata</s>), protector of all wombs (<s>sarvagarbhasaṃrakṣaṇi</s>) — [<s>mantra</s>:] siri-siri bhiri-bhiri miri-miri giri-giri piri-piri — O you who draw in from all directions (<s>samantākarṣaṇi</s>), destroyer of all enemies (<s>sarvaśatrūn pramathani</s>), protect, protect me and all beings always from all fears, from all calamities, from all diseases! — [<s>mantra</s>:] cili-cili viri-viri dhiri-dhiri — O purifier free from obstruction (<s>vigatāvaraṇaviśodhani</s>), destroyer of manifold obstructions (<s>vividhāvaraṇavināśini</s>)! — [<s>mantra</s>:] muci-muci muri-muri muli-muli kili-kili mili-mili — O Lotus One (<s>kamala</s>), immaculate, victorious, bringer of victory (<s>jayavijayāvaha</s>), ever-victorious (<s>jayavati</s>), distinguished one (<s>viśeṣavati</s>), blessed one (<s>bhagavatī</s>), wearer of a jeweled crown and garland (<s>ratnamakuṭamālādhari</s>), wearer of manifold and variegated adornments (<s>bahuvividhavicitraveśadhāriṇi</s>)! O Blessed Great Spell Goddess (<s>bhagavatī mahāvidyā devī</s>), protect, protect me and all beings from all directions, purifier of all sins (<s>sarvapāpaviśodhani</s>)! — [<s>mantra</s>:] hulu-hulu mulu-mulu — protect, protect me and all beings who are helpless, unprotected, without refuge, without shelter, without recourse — liberate them from all sufferings! O Fierce One (<s>caṇḍi</s>), swift one (<s>vegavati</s>), repeller of all evil ones (<s>sarvaduṣṭanivāriṇi</s>), bringer of victory (<s>vijayavāhinī</s>)! — [<s>mantra</s>:] huru-huru curu-curu turu-turu — O protector of life (<s>āyuḥpālini</s>), destroyer of the best of <s>asuras</s> (<s>suravarapramathani</s>), worshipped by all hosts of gods (<s>sarvadevagaṇapūjita</s>)! — [<s>mantra</s>:] ciri-ciri viri-viri — O universally watchful one (<s>samantāvalokita</s>), radiant, supremely radiant, supremely pure in radiance (<s>suprabhaviśuddha</s>), purifier of all sins! — [<s>mantra</s>:] dhuru-dhuru — O bearer of the earth (<s>dharaṇidhara</s>) — dhara-dhara sumuja sumuru-sumuru ru ru cale — set in motion all evil ones, fulfill [all] wishes!
[Manuscript folio Mpv-Dh_132]

children.translated_text: O <s>Māttaṅginī</s>! O bearer of the auspicious body! O victorious lotus! Destroy, destroy! O one with the boon-bestowing goad! <s>Oṃ</s>, O one purified by the lotus, purify, purify! Pure one, pure one! Bear, bear! Fill, fill! Rush, rush! O one purified by auspiciousness! O one of purified face! O sword-bearer, sword-bearer! Scrape, scrape! O blazing-peaked one, blazing-peaked one! O one of radiance seen on all sides! O one purified by excellent splendor! O one of purity illuminating and spreading in every direction! Blaze, blaze! O one who attracts all hosts of gods! O one of truthful vow! <s>Oṃ hrīṃ traṃ</s>, cross over, cross over! Deliver me, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, and all beings! O one beheld by the <s>Nāgas</s>! Quick, quick! Swift, swift! <s>Hulu hulu, hutu hutu, turu turu, tuhu tuhu, kiṇi kiṇi</s>, destroy, destroy! O devourer of all planetary afflictions (<s>graha</s>)! <s>Piṅgari piṅgari</s>, release, release, release, release! <s>Sumu sumu</s>! O well-moving one! Cross over, cross over! O one beheld by the <s>Nāgas</s>, deliver me, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, and all beings from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)! O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, [protect us] from the eight great terrible fears! With the binding of protection in all directions on all sides, with the <s>vajra</s>-noose binding! O <s>vajra</s>-flaming one! O one purified by the <s>vajra</s> flame! Fill, fill! Bear, bear! Rush, rush! O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, purified in the womb! O purifier of the embryo! O filler of the belly! Protect, protect! Blaze, blaze! Move, move! <s>Oṃ</s>, O flaming one! May the gods rain down on all sides with divine waters! O one who rains <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)! O one who causes the deities to descend! Anoint me with the nectar-body of the excellent words of the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One)! Protect, protect me and all beings everywhere, at all times, from all fears, from all calamities, from all terrors of malevolent beings! O purifier of all strife, conflict, and disputes, and of all fears! O purifier of bad dreams, ill omens, inauspiciousness, and sin! O filler of the belly! O destroyer of all <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>! Power, power! O powerful one! Victory, victory! Triumph, triumph! May there be victory everywhere and at all times! May this great <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) be accomplished for me! Accomplish the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle)!
[Mpv-Dh_133]

children.translated_text: Destroy the obstacles! Victory, victory! Succeed, succeed! Awaken, awaken! Fulfill, fulfill! O fulfiller, fulfiller! Fulfill my wishes! O one whose form has arisen from purity! O supreme in victory! O maker of victory! O victorious one! Stand firm, stand firm, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>! Guard the vow (<s>samaya</s>)! O one purified by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Look upon me and all beings! Fulfill all wishes! Of all beings, save me from the eight great terrible fears! Flow, flow! Spread forth, spread forth! O purifier of all obscurations! O one purified in all-pervading form! Departed, departed! O one from whom impurity has departed! O purifier of all impurities! O one purified by all auspiciousness! Destroy, destroy! O purifier of all sins! O one from whom stain has departed! O victorious one! O radiant one! O <s>vajra</s>-one! O <s>vajra</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-one! <s>Oṃ</s>, empowered over the three worlds, <s>svāhā</s>! Crowned by the consecration of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Empowered by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O heart, <s>svāhā</s>! Accomplished in the vow of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Indra</s>-mighty one, O one beheld by <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Brahmā</s>, O one inhabited by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Empowered by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Honored by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one worshipped and honored by <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Empowered by the strength and vigor of <s>Vajradhara</s> and <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Viruḍhaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one honored by the Four Great Kings, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Yama</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one worshipped and honored by <s>Yama</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the followers of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Māruta</s> (Wind), <s>svāhā</s>! To the great <s>Māruta</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>svāhā</s>! To the one beheld by the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of gods (<s>deva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of epilepsy-spirits (<s>apasmāra</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Asuras</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of humans, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of non-humans, <s>svāhā</s>! To all planetary afflictions (<s>graha</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To all constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To all beings (<s>bhūta</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!
[Mpv-Dh_134]

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>! O you of vast womb (<s>vipulagarbha</s>), vast and immaculate (<s>vipulavimala</s>), immaculate-wombed (<s>vimalagarbha</s>), immaculate (<s>vimala</s>), victory-wombed (<s>jayagarbha</s>), diamond-flame-wombed (<s>vajrajvālāgarbha</s>), you who penetrate the depths of movement (<s>gatigahana</s>), purifier of the sky (<s>gaganaviśodhani</s>), purifier of all sins (<s>sarvapāpaviśodhani</s>)! <s>Oṃ</s>! O Virtuous One (<s>guṇavati</s>), sky-wanderer — [<s>mantra</s>:] gaganavicāriṇi-gaganavicāriṇi giri-giri giriṇi-giriṇi gabhari-garddhabhari gamari-gamari gabhari-gabhari gaha-gaha gargāri-gargāri gagari-gagari gaṃbhari-gaṃbhari gabhi-gabhi gahi-gahi gamani-gamani guha-guha guru-guru

body.text: tadyathā om amṛtavare vara-vara pravara viśuddhe hūṃ-hūṃ phaṭ-phaṭ svāhā | om amṛtavilokini garbha saṃrakṣaṇi ākarṣaṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭphaṭ svāhā | aparājitāhṛdayam |

om vimale vipule jayavare jayavāhini amṛtaviraje hūṃ hūṃ phaṭphaṭ svāhā | om bhara-bhara saṃbhara-saṃbhara indriye balaviśodhani hūṃ hūṃ phaṭphaṭru ru cale svāhā | om maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare hūṃ hūṃ phaṭphaṭ svāhā | upahṛdayavidyā |
body.translated_text: [<s>mantra</s>:] oṃ vimale vipule jayavare jayavāhini amṛtaviraje hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | oṃ bhara-bhara saṃbhara-saṃbhara indriye balaviśodhani hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ ru ru cale svāhā | oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | [This is] the subsidiary heart-spell (<s>upahṛdayavidyā</s>).

children.translated_text: By merely hearing this [<s>vidyā</s>], all sins are utterly destroyed.

children.text: yayā yukto vajrakāyo namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By which one endowed [with it] obtains a diamond body (<s>vajrakāya</s>) — homage to her, homage, homage!
Remembering which [<s>vidyā</s>], <s>Rāhula</s>, while still situated in the womb, protected his mother;

children.text: prakṣipte yo viṣanadyāṃ namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When [he was] cast into a poisonous river — homage to her, homage, homage!
She who protected the merchant's son when a cruel serpent was poised to strike;
From the burning of poison ... — homage to her, homage, homage!
The great king <s>Brahmadatta</s>, who as a child was protected by her;
Having conquered his enemy, he became resplendent — homage to her always in [my] mind!
A monk of bad morals, who was sick, by which [<s>vidyā</s>], when it was tied at his throat,

children.text: prāṇāmukto yayai svargaṃ namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though released from his life-breath [i.e., dying], by her [he attained] heaven — homage to her, homage, homage!
When a ship was tossed about in the ocean, [he who was] the protector of the merchants' lives,
Remembering which [<s>vidyā</s>], the caravan-leader was [saved] — homage to her, homage, homage!
By which [<s>vidyā</s>], when it was tied upon his wife, he obtained a son;
The king, with arms outstretched [in joy] — homage to her, homage, homage!
A poor woman, remembering which [<s>vidyā</s>], gave a gold coin (<s>dīnāra</s>) to the <s>Jina</s>;
[And] she became the foremost giver, [honored as] a queen — homage to her, homage, homage!
Which [<s>vidyā</s>], when the lord, bound by the awakened <s>asuras</s>, [placed it] in his crest-jewel ...
<s>Vajrī</s> (<s>Indra</s>) attained victory — homage to her, homage, homage!
By the power contained in which [<s>vidyā</s>] alone, having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),

children.text: mārāñjitvā jinā buddhā namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having conquered the <s>Māras</s>, the <s>Jinas</s> became <s>Buddhas</s> — homage to her, homage, homage!
Even a criminal deserving death, cast into every danger,
Remembering which [<s>vidyā</s>], was completely freed — homage to her, homage, homage!
By which [<s>vidyā</s>], when tied at the throat, one is freed from the danger of the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>);
He became the leader of the city — homage to her, homage, homage!
This invincible (<s>aparājitā</s>) <s>vidyā</s> (spell), held by all the <s>Buddhas</s>,
Sealed, spoken, constantly recited, and taught to others;
Written down, rejoiced in, always worshipped for the benefit of beings;

children.text: smṛtvā kāyagatāṃ kṛtvā namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Remembering it and making it body-borne — homage to her, homage, homage!
Even the mere hearing of which is rare in the three worlds,
And its recitation and study [even rarer] — homage to her, homage, homage!
This <s>vidyā</s>, rare, prophesied and praised by the <s>Buddhas</s>,
Renowned as the great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, destroyer of all sins;
Of great power, great potency, great splendor, great radiance,
The <s>vidyā</s> of great virtue, destroyer of all <s>Māras</s>;
Breaker of the bonds of sin, dispeller of the pride of <s>Māra</s>,
Mother of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, destroyer of all evil ones;
Protectress, nourisher, sustainer, destroyer of hostile spells,
She who shatters the mixtures of <s>kākhorda</s> poisons — the auspicious one;
For those devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, for those who receive [it], for those who write [it],
For those who constantly recite and study [it], for those who hold [it], and for those who listen [to it],

children.text: parebhyo diśatāṃ caiva nityaṃ manasi bhāvitām |
children.translated_text: For those who teach it to others, and for those who constantly contemplate it in their minds,
Making it into a manuscript, worshipping and honoring [it] with prostrations;
She who removes all sins, the auspicious one, who fulfills the accumulation [of merit] for awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>);
Homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage!
By the power of whose <s>mantra</s>, all fears and calamities,
Evil <s>asuras</s> and humans, <s>daityas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>,
Planetary spirits (<s>grahas</s>), <s>skandas</s>, epilepsy demons (<s>apasmāras</s>), <s>piśācas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>,

children.text: ḍākinyaḥ śākinīsaṃghā nāgāḥ kāṣordda tu vyādhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, hosts of <s>śākinīs</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>kākhorda</s> diseases,
Fevers, various diseases, and those caused by hostile sorcery,
Poisons, fire, weapons, [hostile] spells, lightning, untimely afflictions,
Excessive rain, drought, and all dangers from enemies —
And also other calamities — [all] are destroyed, there is no doubt;
All undertakings are accomplished — homage to her, homage, homage!

children.text: yaśca tāṃ dhārayet vidyāṃ kaṇṭhe vāhau ca mastake |
children.translated_text: And whoever wears this <s>vidyā</s> at the throat, on the arm, or on the head,
The <s>devas</s>, <s>daityas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and humans always protect him;
<s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s>,
<s>Ḍākinīs</s>, <s>rākṣasīs</s>, <s>dūtīs</s> (female messengers), <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>kaṭapūtanās</s>;

children.text: trisandhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhet nityaṃ buddhārakṣanti taṃ sadā |
children.translated_text: Whoever recites [it] constantly at the three junctures [of the day], the <s>Buddhas</s> always protect him;
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural power,
<s>Yogins</s>, masters of accomplished <s>mantras</s>, great sages of great power —
And <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lord of the <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) together with the thirty [gods], ||
the four great kings (<s>mahārāja</s>), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Nandikeśa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, and <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>, ||
the <s>Bhairavas</s>, the <s>Mātṛkās</s> (Mother goddesses), <s>Durgā</s>, and also others of <s>Māra</s>'s host,
the spell-goddesses (<s>vidyādevī</s>) of great vigor, of great strength and prowess, ||
<s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Āṅkuśī</s>, <s>Vajraśṛṅkhalā</s>,
<s>Mahāśvetā</s>, <s>Mahākālī</s>, <s>Vajradūtī</s>, and <s>Upāśikā</s>, ||
<s>Vajramālā</s>, <s>Mahāvidyā</s>, <s>Suvīryā</s>, <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>,
<s>Vajrāparājitā</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Kālakarṇā</s>, <s>Mahābalā</s>,
and also <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Mahābhāgā</s>, and <s>Padmakuṇḍalī</s>, ||
<s>Maṇicūḍā</s>, <s>Puṣpadantī</s>, <s>Svarṇakeśī</s>, and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
<s>Ekajaṭā</s>, the great goddess, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Vidyutsumālinī</s>, ||
<s>Kapālinī</s>, <s>Laṅkeśī</s>, <s>Kṣudrākṣī</s> — these, the sole leaders —
<s>Hārītī</s>, <s>Pāñcikā</s>, and also <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> and <s>Kūṭadantinī</s>,
<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Siddheśvarī</s>, ever-accompanying. ||

children.text: tamevānye 'pi rakṣanti yasya vidyā kare sthitā |
children.translated_text: These and others also protect the one in whose hand the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) is placed;
that person becomes one striving for the liberation of all beings. ||
Kings become subject to him, and he increases his heap of merit (<s>puṇya</s>);
all rites are accomplished, and he is [as one who has] entered the shrine of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). ||
At the end, he attains the state of a <s>Buddha</s>, in accordance with the word of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: yā strī dhārayed vidyāṃ prasūyedgurviṇī sukham ||
children.translated_text: A woman who bears this <s>vidyā</s>, when pregnant, will give birth with ease; ||
if childless, she obtains a son; freed from disease, she enjoys happiness;
endowed with wealth, grain, and excellent boons, she becomes honored and sweet-spoken. ||
She makes good dreams come true and attains the field of the <s>Jina</s> (Buddha-land).

children.text: ityavocad bhagavān sā ca sarvāvatī parṣadabhyanandan || iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and all of that assembly rejoiced. || Thus: ||

body.translated_text: The Noble Great Amulet Spell-<s>Dhāraṇī</s> (<s>Āryamahāpratisarāvidyādhāraṇī</s>) is complete. ||
